items.review_rationale: Read the Grothendieck K-zero presentation on finite projective classes and direct-sum relations, also described by split short exact sequences. Distinguished K-zero from the group of all finitely generated modules.

references.phrase: isomorphism class of finite projective module
references.context: Algebraic K-theory: isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective modules

references.phrase: abelian group presentation by direct sums
references.context: Algebraic K-theory: group generated by projective module classes modulo [P⊕Q]=[P]+[Q]

references.disposition: For projective quotient modules the short exact sequence splits; relation here is direct-sum additivity.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the valuative diagram and uniqueness-only lifting requirement. For every valuation ring and maps from its generic spectrum and full spectrum, at most one map to X must complete the triangles; existence is not assumed.

references.context: Algebraic geometry: compatibility of maps Spec(K)→X, Spec(V)→S and Spec(V)→X over a base

references.disposition: Only uniqueness is asserted; the condition does not require existence of a lift.

items.review_rationale: Read the rational polynomial eventually equal to length of the nth graded m-adic piece of a finite module over a Noetherian local ring. This polynomial differs from the cumulative Hilbert–Samuel length polynomial.

references.context: Commutative algebra: associated graded pieces of the maximal ideal filtration
Algebra: polynomial with rational coefficients used for eventual equality

references.disposition: This is eventual equality; no assertion is made for small n or that it equals a cumulative Hilbert–Samuel function.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the cumulative m-adic quotient M/m^{n+1}M and its module length at nonnegative n, distinguishing it from the length of a single m-adic graded layer.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient by powers of maximal ideal acting on a module

references.disposition: The stated function is defined for all nonnegative integers and does not itself assert a rational polynomial equality.
